step1_analysis.description: This bipolar sub-circuit features a differential pair (Q1, Q2) with their collectors tied together to a common node (n0), which effectively cancels out the differential fundamental frequency and sums the common-mode or 2nd harmonic currents. The signal at n0 is then buffered by two identical emitter followers (Q3, Q4) to drive the outputs.

paper_reference.title: A Monolithic Double-Balanced Direct Conversion Mixer With an Integrated Wideband Passive Balun

Conversion_Gain.description: Voltage gain from the input to the output at the desired frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Using a generic NPN model at 1.8V, the gain is determined by the transconductance of Q1/Q2 and the load resistors R3/R4. Assuming gm ~ 10mA/26mV and Rload = 1k, intrinsic gain could be high, but tied collectors reduce differential gain to 0. Single-ended gain is expected around 10-15 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for 1.8V supply and generic silicon NPN parameters compared to the high-frequency GaAs HBT process.

Bandwidth.description: The 3-dB bandwidth of the amplifier/buffer stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: Silicon NPNs in standard CMOS processes typically have lower fT than GaAs HBTs. Expected bandwidth is limited by parasitic capacitances at node n0.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard generic NPN models or parasitic BJTs in 130nm CMOS typically achieve a few GHz bandwidth, significantly lower than the 40 GHz of the specialized GaAs process.

Power_Consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the sub-circuit.

paper_reported.value: Not explicitly stated for this sub-block

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming bias currents of ~1mA per branch (tail current 2mA, emitter followers 1mA each, bias mirror 1mA), total current is ~5mA. At 1.8V, power is 5mA * 1.8V = 9mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on standard biasing for 1k ohm loads and 1.8V supply to keep transistors in the active region.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, 3dB bandwidth, and transient output swing of the bipolar sub-circuit. Resistor values (1k and 100 ohms) have been appended to the netlist to allow simulation.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Bipolar Mixer Sub-circuit

.model npn npn (is=1e-16 bf=100 vaf=50 cjc=1p cje=2p fT=10G)

* DUT with appended resistor values
Q1 n0 label_net_0 n5 npn
Q2 n0 label_net_1 n2 npn
R1 n2 n3 100
R2 n3 n5 100
Q3 label_net_2 n0 n8 npn
Q4 label_net_3 n0 n7 npn
R3 n0 label_net_4 1k
Q5 n1 n1 n6 npn
R4 n0 label_net_5 1k
R5 n7 label_net_6 1k
R6 n1 label_net_7 1k
R7 n8 label_net_8 1k
R8 n4 0 100
R9 n6 0 100
Q6 n3 n1 n4 npn

* Supply and Bias Sources
V_label_net_2 label_net_2 0 dc 1.8
V_label_net_3 label_net_3 0 dc 1.8
V_label_net_4 label_net_4 0 dc 1.8
V_label_net_5 label_net_5 0 dc 1.8
V_label_net_7 label_net_7 0 dc 1.8

V_label_net_6 label_net_6 0 dc 0
V_label_net_8 label_net_8 0 dc 0

* Input Sources (Single-ended drive to observe gain at common node n0)
V_label_net_0 label_net_0 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 sin(0.9 0.05 10Meg)
V_label_net_1 label_net_1 0 dc 0.9 ac 0

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let total_current = -(i(V_label_net_2) + i(V_label_net_3) + i(V_label_net_4) + i(V_label_net_5) + i(V_label_net_7))
let power_consumption = total_current * 1.8
print power_consumption

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 20 1Meg 100Gig
let gain_db = vdb(n8)
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=(max_gain-3) fall=1
print max_gain bw_3db

* 3. Transient Analysis for Output Swing
tran 1n 200n
meas tran v_max max v(n8)
meas tran v_min min v(n8)
let output_swing = v_max - v_min
print output_swing

quit
.endc
.end
